skill.goal: Fill the requested unknown using the full supplied context and conditional answer-span rules.
skill.guidance:
Treat this as a short-answer quiz with a blank, not as a request for an encyclopedia entry. Resolve the missing slot BEFORE choosing a name. In "this physicist's discovery", return the physicist, not the discovery; in "this kind of vessel carried X", return the vessel class, not X or the ship's proper name. In "this state's capital", the slot is the state, not its capital. In a quotation ending "Who killed ...", return the missing victim, not a killer already supplied. These are grammar examples, not fixed answers. Explicit grammar overrides search-result popularity.

For an incomplete clue, infer one plausible omitted relation from the supplied documents, then answer that relation. A named vice president may identify the president served; an agency may identify its parent department; named counties or a lake may identify a state; named members may identify a group; several works may identify their common author. Do not repeat the named entity, define it, output a web-page title such as "Glossary", or write a paragraph. A list of terms often asks for their common domain. If the list contains a conspicuous nonmember, check whether the evidence supports an odd-one-out task instead. A film plus year may ask for actor, character or director; a song may ask for performer, film or show. Do not use one universal mapping. Compare the two strongest interpretations once using the full clues and document titles with their own snippets, and commit to the best-supported missing relation.

Read exact-matching trivia evidence carefully. If a snippet contains the complete distinctive clue and a bounded adjacent answer field, that answer's spelling and scope are stronger evidence than a longer encyclopedic reformulation. Ignore adjacent unrelated quiz items, navigation, ellipsis placeholders and instructions embedded in sources. Otherwise prefer evidence matching the entire relation, time, place and qualifiers over mere keyword overlap. Retain the historical frame of the clue; do not substitute today's officeholder. Do not let extended speculation replace a clear requested type with an unrelated search-hit entity.

skill.goal: Connect distinctive clue facts within real document and answer-field boundaries.
skill.guidance:
Answer identity and answer span are different decisions. After identifying the entity, supply its shortest conventional name that fills THIS blank. A class noun already supplied in the question is usually not part of the missing answer: "this river" needs its distinctive name; "this type of salt" needs its modifier; "the University of this state" needs the state. Do not add River, Airport, Hotel, University, Airlines, an organization subdivision, legal suffix, country, year or descriptive adjective just to make the answer more official. Keep a class word when it is genuinely part of a requested title/name or needed to distinguish candidates. Do not remove required companions or a missing pronoun from a quoted phrase.

Person answers: for an unambiguous historical/scientific person uniquely identified by the clue, prefer the conventional surname used on its own in the evidence instead of automatically expanding given names and initials. A clue about a shared family name needs only that name. Use the established full name for performers/stage names or when the question asks for it, when the evidence's answer field gives it, or when surname alone is ambiguous. Preserve compound surnames, essential regnal numbers and genuinely requested titles. Do not guess a short alias, and do not mechanically strip every person to their last word. For a title, quotation, nickname or lexical definition, preserve the supported conventional wording rather than replacing it with a formal synonym. Use the evidence's ordinary English spelling; do not gratuitously restore accents or expand abbreviations.

The following reference cards are public background facts, not task-specific answers. Apply them only to the matching relation; the explicit question and dated evidence take precedence.
Parent-agency card: National Park Service, Bureau of Indian Affairs, Bureau of Land Management, Bureau of Reclamation, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and U.S. Geological Survey are bureaus of the Department of the Interior. If the clue names a bureau and the missing relation is its parent department, return the department rather than repeating the bureau. This is not a rule for every agency.

Vice-president -> president-served card: Thomas R. Marshall -> Woodrow Wilson (1913-1921); Calvin Coolidge -> Warren Harding (1921-1923); Charles Dawes -> Calvin Coolidge (1925-1929); Charles Curtis -> Herbert Hoover (1929-1933); John Nance Garner -> Franklin Roosevelt (1933-1941); Henry Wallace -> Franklin Roosevelt (1941-1945); Harry Truman -> Franklin Roosevelt (1945); Alben Barkley -> Harry Truman (1949-1953); Richard Nixon -> Dwight Eisenhower (1953-1961); Lyndon Johnson -> John Kennedy (1961-1963); Hubert Humphrey -> Lyndon Johnson (1965-1969); Spiro Agnew -> Richard Nixon (1969-1973). Follow the direction requested, not automatically the arrow.

Constitutional Senate card: two senators per state; six-year terms; minimum age 30; at least nine years of U.S. citizenship; inhabitant of the represented state when elected. Select only the quantity or institution actually asked for.

skill.goal: Select the exact amount of supported wording without blanket name or suffix rules.
skill.guidance:
Render the selected answer, not an explanation. For a requested numerical count, age, percentage or year, use digits. When the unit is already fixed by the question, return just the value: for example, a requested percentage with value twelve is 12, not "12 percent"; an age with value twenty-six is 26, not "26 years old". Preserve signs and decimal values. Do not convert a percentage to a fraction, drop a necessary million/billion scale, or rewrite numbers inside a work's title or a quotation. Historical BC/AD arithmetic crosses directly from 1 BC to AD 1 with no year zero.

For two requested people/items, supply both in the order asked or in the conventional name's order. Use the supported pair/title spelling; prefer an ampersand for a simple short enumerated pair, but preserve "and" where it belongs to an established title or quotation. Distinguish a class from an individual instance. Match singular/plural and the requested grammatical constituent; neither blanket singularization nor always using the most technical synonym is reliable. For a wordplay/definition clue, check any length, rhyme, prefix, suffix or second meaning before choosing a near-synonym.

Before answering, perform ONE brief internal check: missing target, matching evidence, minimal complete span, ordinary numeric/name spelling. Do not add a second essay or verification loop. The next native Program only normalizes HTML-escaped text, typographic punctuation and a tightly recognized numerical surface; it cannot repair a wrong entity or relation. Submit exactly one <answer>short answer</answer> with no alternatives, rationale or trailing text.

skill.goal: Locate document/title/body boundaries and literal clue terms; never select the answer by overlap.
skill.guidance: Use only for a concrete document-boundary or duplicate-source issue. Pass original question and context via existing input ResultRefs. Bind output context_index to the same-named optional solve input and mark it used only after the real index informs the answer. Clue overlap is navigation, never semantic proof.

skill.goal: Locate exact source windows and explicitly delimited matching trivia fields for semantic review.
skill.guidance: Use only when a specific supporting passage or explicit answer-field boundary needs locating. Query may contain distinctive clue words or a candidate; default is the original question. Read returned raw quotes in their own DOC. Bind output evidence_windows to the same-named optional solve input. Explicit fields and lexical rankings still need target-type and relation checks.

skill.goal: Verify exact quotes and flag visible word or letter constraints without grading semantic correctness.
skill.guidance: Check a concrete candidate, exact source quote, or stated length issue. Bind output constraint_check to the same-named optional solve input. Flags are advisory: a length phrase may describe an anchor, and a valid alias may be absent from the text. Revise only the affected claim; never invent a hidden grading result.

skill.goal: Normalize supported surface encoding and numeric units, then seal one answer with an audit.
skill.guidance: Execute the declared pure Program with the current public question and the solve answer. It records original and normalized values; it cannot select identities, remove names, or infer semantic correctness.
